title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Proposition 3 from the previous page, on an elliptic curve E over a field k of characteristic ≠ 2. The curve is written in the form X'^2 = X^3 + a1 X^2 + a2 X + a3. Grothendieck writes p (Weierstrass ℘) for the x-coordinate and p' for the y-coordinate.

The claim: for x, y, z ∈ E(k)∖{0}, pairwise distinct, x+y+z = 0 if and only if det[[1, p(x), p'(x)], [1, p(y), p'(y)], [1, p(z), p'(z)]] = 0. In other words, the three points sum to zero exactly when they are collinear in the plane cubic model. This is the chord construction of the group law.

Forward direction:
- From the previous page, x+y+z = 0 means {x}+{y}+{z} is linearly equivalent to 3{0}.
- So there is a rational function f in L(3·0) = span(1, p, p') with exactly a triple pole at 0. Its coefficient on p' is therefore nonzero.
- "OPS" stands for "on peut supposer" (one may assume). After scaling, f = p' + αp + β with div f = {x}+{y}+{z} − 3{0_E}; this is (43).
- Hence f(x) = f(y) = f(z) = 0, which is (44)/(45).
- So the column (p'(x), p'(y), p'(z)) is a linear combination of the columns (p(x), p(y), p(z)) and (1, 1, 1). This gives the vanishing determinant (42).

Converse:
- Assume x, y, z are pairwise distinct and (42) holds.
- Then p(x) = p(y) = p(z) is impossible, since a fibre of the degree-2 map p: E → P^1 has at most 2 points.
- So (1,1,1) and (p(x), p(y), p(z)) are linearly independent, and (42) yields α, β with (45).
- Then f = p' + αp + β is a degree-3 function vanishing at the three distinct points x, y, z. Hence div f = {x}+{y}+{z} − 3{0}, which gives (41).

Purpose: an explicit, coordinate-based setup of the group law. The next page uses it to derive the chord formulas (slope λ, intercept μ, and the cubic (48) in z0). This serves the study of moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2.
errors: No mathematical errors. The converse silently uses x, y, z ≠ 0, which is assumed in the statement on the previous page. The heavily crossed passage shows Grothendieck reworking the hypothesis from something like 'not all equal' to 'pairwise distinct', and adding the justification that p(x) = p(y) = p(z) cannot occur. The final argument is correct.

ideas.what: Three distinct nonzero points sum to zero iff the determinant of the rows (1, ℘, ℘') vanishes, i.e. the points are collinear; proved via Riemann–Roch for L(3·0) = <1, ℘, ℘'> and linear equivalence of divisors.
ideas.modern_name: Chord-tangent group law / collinearity criterion on a Weierstrass cubic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Newton, Jacobi, Poincaré; the ℘-function version is due to Weierstrass/Frobenius–Stickelberger)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, textbook-level proof of the collinearity criterion for the group law on an elliptic curve. It is an expository part of Grothendieck's notes on moduli of elliptic curves, with nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'OPS' at the top is the abbreviation 'On peut supposer' (one may assume).

In the crossed-out region the marginal insertion appears to read roughly 'x,y,z deux à deux distincts' and 'alors on n'a pas p(x)=p(y)=p(z) (sinon ...)'. The phrase transcribed as 'fixons[?] p, deux à deux[?]' is mostly struck-out text and should not be read as part of the final argument.
'cela implique' after the column vectors reads 'ce qui implique'.
